about: The fresh-paper questions: 8 per paper, written from each PDF's pdftotext (plain and -layout) only, before any answer, in the library wording (no table, figure or section numbers; a subject phrase naming the paper's subject where the question would fit other library papers). Where a paper prints one usable table, the second table question is a second lookup (C2).

fresh/gasification/C1.q: In the carbide slag-assisted steam gasification of sewage sludge, what N2 flow rate, steam flow rate and isothermal reaction time were used in each run?
fresh/gasification/C1.expect: N2 800 mL/min, steam 1.0 g/min, 30 min isothermal (sec. 2.2)
fresh/gasification/C1.trap: the 105 °C / 24 h drying, or 3.0 kg H2O per kg SS

fresh/gasification/B1.q: In the carbide slag-assisted steam gasification of sewage sludge, what apparent retention rate did Cr have at Ca/C = 0?

fresh/gasification/T1.q: What ash and fixed carbon contents, on an air-dried basis, did the sewage sludge used for carbide slag-assisted steam gasification have?

fresh/gasification/T2.q: What SiO2 and MgO contents did XRF give for the carbide slag used in the steam gasification of sewage sludge?

fresh/gasification/X1.q: In the carbide slag-assisted steam gasification of sewage sludge at 700 °C, by what percentage did the H2 yield rise when Ca/C went from 0 to 0.75?
fresh/gasification/X1.trap: the H2 volume fraction's 57.73 to 68.02 (10.29 points)

fresh/gasification/H1.q: Which Ca/C ratio was chosen for the temperature experiments of the carbide slag-assisted sewage sludge steam gasification, and how much carbide slag did that ratio take per 10.0 g of sludge?

fresh/gasification/F1.q: Why did carbide slag addition lower the RAC risk level of As from medium to low in the sewage sludge gasification residues?
fresh/gasification/F1.expect: It did not: As stayed at medium RAC risk at every Ca/C ratio; CS was largely ineffective for As (abstract, sec. 3.2)
fresh/gasification/F1.trap: explaining an As drop to low risk (Zn and Cd fell from high to medium)

fresh/gasification/A1.q: What tar yield did the carbide slag-assisted steam gasification of sewage sludge give at Ca/C = 0.50?
fresh/gasification/A1.expect: Not given: tar yield was not quantified (secs. 3.1, 3.3)
fresh/gasification/A1.trap: a gas yield (e.g. total gas yield) given as the tar yield

fresh/techno-economic/C1.q: In the CO2-WAG enhanced oil recovery study with stacking-learning proxy models, how many injection and production wells does the reservoir sector have, and how much remaining oil does it hold?
fresh/techno-economic/C1.expect: 19 injection wells, 10 production wells, 3.5 billion barrels of remaining oil (sec. 2)

fresh/techno-economic/B1.q: What mutation rate and mutation step did the NSGA-II algorithm use in the multiobjective CO2-WAG optimization with stacking-learning proxies?

fresh/techno-economic/T1.q: What average porosity and initial reservoir pressure does the reservoir model of the CO2-WAG stacking-learning optimization have?

fresh/techno-economic/T2.q: How many Pareto front solutions did the decision tree place in the silver and in the bronze clusters in the CO2-WAG stacking-learning optimization?

fresh/techno-economic/X1.q: In the CO2-WAG stacking-learning optimization, what share of the Pareto front solutions fell in the black cluster?

fresh/techno-economic/H1.q: In the CO2-WAG stacking-learning study, which of the three base proxy models had the lowest MSE over the whole data bank, and how many hidden layers and neurons does it have?
fresh/techno-economic/H1.expect: the second base model (Logsig), MSE 0.00961; three layers of 22, 20 and 9 neurons (Table 6, sec. 2.4)
fresh/techno-economic/H1.trap: the Tansig model's two layers of 24 and 14, or Softmax's 28 and 10

fresh/techno-economic/F1.q: Why did the NSGA-II algorithm in the CO2-WAG stacking-learning optimization produce only 60 solutions on its Pareto front?
fresh/techno-economic/F1.expect: It did not: it produced 500 Pareto front solutions, of which 60 were classified gold (abstract, Table 11)
fresh/techno-economic/F1.trap: explaining why the front holds only 60 solutions

fresh/techno-economic/A1.q: What discount rate was used to compute the NPV in the CO2-WAG stacking-learning optimization?
fresh/techno-economic/A1.expect: Not given: D is defined as the discount rate in the NPV equation, but no value is stated (CAPEX $300 million, oil $60/bbl, $8/ton reward, water $8/bbl are)
fresh/techno-economic/A1.trap: the 10% recovery factor or another stated number given as the rate

fresh/catalytic/C1.q: In the one-step co-reduction synthesis of magnetically recyclable Ni–Ag/rGO for 4-nitrophenol reduction, at what pH, temperature and time did the reduction with hydrazine hydrate run?
fresh/catalytic/C1.trap: the vacuum drying at 80 °C for 12 h, or 30 min sonication

fresh/catalytic/B1.q: What saturation and remanent magnetization did the Ni–Ag/rGO catalyst for 4-nitrophenol reduction have?
fresh/catalytic/B1.trap: pure Ni's 39.52 and 4.59 emu/g, or the 31.81 emu/g estimated for its Ni

fresh/catalytic/T1.q: In the comparison of 4-nitrophenol reduction catalysts made for the Ni–Ag/rGO study, what rate constant k and normalized rate constant K does Ag/g-C3N4 have?
fresh/catalytic/T1.expect: k 0.75 min−1, K 7.5 min−1 mg−1 mL, at 0.1 mg/mL (Table 1)

fresh/catalytic/C2.q: What 4-nitrophenol degradation efficiencies did the Ni–Ag/rGO catalyst reach in the first and in the tenth recycling run?
fresh/catalytic/C2.expect: 97.17% in the first, 89.57% in the tenth (sec. 3.3)
fresh/catalytic/C2.trap: "more than 90% of its activity" from the abstract

fresh/catalytic/X1.q: For 4-nitrophenol reduction, how many times larger is the rate constant of Ni–Ag/rGO with 0.1 wt% rGO than that of the Ni–Ag catalyst without rGO?
fresh/catalytic/X1.trap: the 3.4 times stated for 0.5 wt% rGO

fresh/catalytic/H1.q: Which rGO content gave the Ni–Ag/rGO catalyst its highest 4-nitrophenol reduction rate constant, and what volume of rGO solution was added in the synthesis to reach that content?
fresh/catalytic/H1.expect: 0.5 wt% rGO (k 0.8585 min−1); 1 mL of rGO solution (volumes 0, 0.2, 1, 2 mL give 0.0, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0 wt%) (secs. 2.2, 3.2)

fresh/catalytic/F1.q: Why did the Ni–Ag/rGO catalyst with 1.0 wt% rGO reach the highest rate constant for 4-nitrophenol reduction?
fresh/catalytic/F1.expect: It did not: 1.0 wt% gave the lowest, 0.1375 min−1; 0.5 wt% was highest at 0.8585 min−1 (Table 1, sec. 3.2)
fresh/catalytic/F1.trap: explaining why more rGO gave the fastest reduction

fresh/catalytic/A1.q: What BET specific surface area did the Ni–Ag/rGO catalyst for 4-nitrophenol reduction have?
fresh/catalytic/A1.expect: Not given: no BET or surface-area measurement is reported
fresh/catalytic/A1.trap: a particle size (60-70 nm) or another number given as the area

fresh/adsorption/C1.q: In the study of coal permeability and adsorption capacity after oxidation for coalbed methane, which oxidant was used, at what concentration and for how long?
fresh/adsorption/C1.trap: H2O2, NaClO, KMnO4 or ClO2 from earlier studies

fresh/adsorption/B1.q: In the coal oxidation study for coalbed methane, what contact angle did sample HRC-SX-C have before oxidation?
fresh/adsorption/B1.trap: the 120-135° range of the other samples, or 82-130° after oxidation

fresh/adsorption/T1.q: What NMR porosity did coal sample MRC-SX-A have before and after the oxidation treatment for coalbed methane?

fresh/adsorption/T2.q: In the coal oxidation study for coalbed methane, what specific surface area did sample LRC-XJ-A have before and after oxidation?

fresh/adsorption/X1.q: In the coal oxidation study for coalbed methane, what was the mean change in specific surface area over the samples whose pore structure was measured before and after oxidation?
fresh/adsorption/X1.trap: the 72.20% average fall in adsorption capacity

fresh/adsorption/H1.q: Which coal sample had the largest porosity increase after the oxidation treatment for coalbed methane, and what moisture and ash contents did it have?

fresh/adsorption/F1.q: Why did oxidation raise the adsorption capacity of the coal samples by 72.20% on average in the coalbed methane study?
fresh/adsorption/F1.expect: It did not: adsorption capacity fell by 72.20% on average, with lower contact angle and specific surface area (abstract)

fresh/adsorption/A1.q: What vitrinite reflectance did the coal samples of the oxidation study for coalbed methane have?
fresh/adsorption/A1.expect: Not given: only moisture and ash (Table 1) and basin of origin are stated
fresh/adsorption/A1.trap: a moisture, ash or porosity value given as reflectance

fresh/pyrolysis/C1.q: How was the corn straw–oil sludge composite pellet fuel made: at what corn straw to oil sludge mass ratio, and into pellets of what diameter and length?
fresh/pyrolysis/C1.expect: 1.5:1 (60/40 w/w); cylindrical pellets 6 mm in diameter and 20 mm long (sec. 2.1)
fresh/pyrolysis/C1.trap: the 150 mesh (0.106 mm) sieve size or 10% water content

fresh/pyrolysis/B1.q: In the co-pyrolysis of corn straw and oil sludge pellets, what maximum did the deviation between the experimental and calculated TG curves reach, and at about what temperature?
fresh/pyrolysis/B1.trap: the 170-650 °C core stage given as the temperature

fresh/pyrolysis/T1.q: What K2O and Fe2O3 contents did the corn straw fuel and the corn straw–oil sludge composite fuel have?
fresh/pyrolysis/T1.expect: corn straw fuel K2O 31.94, Fe2O3 4.67 wt %; composite fuel K2O 7.35, Fe2O3 20.80 wt % (Table 2)

fresh/pyrolysis/T2.q: At a heating rate of 20 °C/min, what initial and burnout temperatures did the corn straw–oil sludge composite pellet fuel have?
fresh/pyrolysis/T2.trap: the corn straw fuel's 254.0 / 480.5, or CF at 10 or 30 °C/min

fresh/pyrolysis/X1.q: In the kinetics of corn straw and corn straw–oil sludge pellet fuels, by what percentage did the composite fuel's mean FWO activation energy exceed the corn straw fuel's?
fresh/pyrolysis/X1.trap: the KAS means 194.70 / 207.44 (6.54%) or a single α

fresh/pyrolysis/H1.q: Of the corn straw fuel and the corn straw–oil sludge composite fuel, which had the higher maximum weight loss rate at 30 °C/min, and what higher heating value does that fuel have?
fresh/pyrolysis/H1.expect: the corn straw fuel (SF), 27.62 %/min against 19.71; HHV 17.20 MJ/kg (Tables 4 and 1)
fresh/pyrolysis/H1.trap: the composite fuel's 21.96 MJ/kg, or oil sludge's 33.97

fresh/pyrolysis/F1.q: Why was the corn straw–oil sludge composite fuel made with 60% oil sludge?
fresh/pyrolysis/F1.expect: It was not: it holds 40% oil sludge (corn straw/oil sludge 60/40); more than 40% oil sludge gave ash above 12% and poor durability (sec. 2.1)

fresh/pyrolysis/A1.q: What bio-oil yield did the pyrolysis of the corn straw–oil sludge composite pellet fuel give?
fresh/pyrolysis/A1.expect: Not given: the study is thermogravimetric; product yields were not measured
fresh/pyrolysis/A1.trap: a weight loss (85-90%) or M∞ given as the oil yield

fresh/co2-capture/C1.q: In the review of hydrate-based CO2 capture for CCUS, what hydrate dissociation temperature and CO2 hydrate dissociation enthalpy does its Aspen Plus process simulation assume?
fresh/co2-capture/C1.trap: the 10 °C minimum temperature difference or COP of 3

fresh/co2-capture/B1.q: What second-law (exergy) efficiency did the Aspen Plus simulation of hydrate-based CO2 capture in the hydrate CCUS review reach?

fresh/co2-capture/T1.q: In the flue gas of the hydrate-based CO2 capture simulation in the hydrate CCUS review, what are the CO2 mole fraction and its feed rate in kmol/h?
fresh/co2-capture/T1.trap: N2's 0.71 and 31,697 kmol/h, or the 16% CO2 in sec. 5.3

fresh/co2-capture/T2.q: In the Aspen Plus hydrate-based CO2 capture simulation of the hydrate CCUS review, what discharge pressure does the third compressor have, and to what temperature do the refrigeration units cool the hot stream?

fresh/co2-capture/X1.q: In the flue gas of the hydrate-based CO2 capture simulation in the hydrate CCUS review, what share of the CO2 plus N2 feed, by mass, is CO2?

fresh/co2-capture/H1.q: In the hydrate CCUS review's process simulation, to what pressure does the first-stage compressor raise the flue gas, and what temperature does the gas reach there?

fresh/co2-capture/F1.q: Why are the two flue gas compression stages in the hydrate CCUS review's simulation taken as isothermal?
fresh/co2-capture/F1.expect: They are not: both stages are adiabatic (isentropic), with an efficiency of 0.8 (sec. 5.2, Table 4)

fresh/co2-capture/A1.q: What CO2 purity does the product gas reach in the hydrate CCUS review's own Aspen Plus simulation of two-stage hydrate-based CO2 separation?
fresh/co2-capture/A1.expect: Not given: the simulation section states energy (74.15%) and exergy (38.85%) efficiencies, not product purity
fresh/co2-capture/A1.trap: the 16% or 0.19 feed CO2, or another study's recovery (92%, 92.17%)

fresh/wastewater-treatment/C1.q: In the review of magnetic iron oxide nanoparticles in mixed matrix membranes for wastewater, what tensile strength increase and river-water bacteria removal did the bacterial cellulose acetate membrane with Fe3O4 from pineapple biowaste reach?
fresh/wastewater-treatment/C1.expect: tensile strength up to 73%; bacteria removal 67.4% (Suryanto et al.)

fresh/wastewater-treatment/B1.q: In the review of magnetic iron oxide nanoparticles in mixed matrix membranes for wastewater, what BSA rejection and flux recovery ratio did the GO/Fe3O4/PES membrane show?
fresh/wastewater-treatment/B1.expect: about 92% BSA rejection, 87.9% flux recovery ratio
fresh/wastewater-treatment/B1.trap: its 76.2% PWF increase, 35% WCA decrease or 53.9° contact angle

fresh/wastewater-treatment/T1.q: What density and Curie temperature does the review of magnetic iron oxide nanoparticles in mixed matrix membranes give for hematite?
fresh/wastewater-treatment/T1.trap: magnetite's 5.18 and 850 K, maghemite's 4.87 and 820-986 K

fresh/wastewater-treatment/T2.q: In the review of magnetic iron oxide nanoparticles for wastewater membranes, what adsorption capacities are listed for Pb(II) and Cd(II) on the CuFe2O4/sepiolite/graphene oxide composite?

fresh/wastewater-treatment/X1.q: In the review of magnetic iron oxide nanoparticles in mixed matrix membranes, by what factor did the Fe3O4/PVP nanocomposite raise the water flux of the PES nanofiltration membrane?

fresh/wastewater-treatment/H1.q: Which iron oxide does the review of magnetic iron oxide nanoparticles in mixed matrix membranes describe as a base material for preparing Fe3O4 and γ-Fe2O3, and what melting point does it list for it?

fresh/wastewater-treatment/F1.q: Why did adding 0.2 wt% magnetic Fe2O3 nanoparticles to PVDF lower the water flux by 20% in the oily wastewater membrane described in the iron oxide mixed matrix membrane review?
fresh/wastewater-treatment/F1.expect: It did not: the flux rose to 46 L m−2 h−1, 20% higher than neat PVDF, with oil rejection above 94% (Esmail et al.)

fresh/wastewater-treatment/A1.q: What cost per square metre of membrane does the review of magnetic iron oxide nanoparticles in mixed matrix membranes give for magnetic MMMs?
fresh/wastewater-treatment/A1.expect: Not given: the review calls methods cost-effective or costly but states no membrane cost
fresh/wastewater-treatment/A1.trap: a flux or capacity number given as a cost

fresh/crystallization/C1.q: In making the Sn-incorporated Ge2Sb2Te5 (GST) thin films for terahertz sensing, what sputtering power went to the GST target, what powers to the Sn target, and how thick were the films?
fresh/crystallization/C1.expect: GST 50 W; Sn 0, 12 and 24 W; about 500 nm (sec. 2)
fresh/crystallization/C1.trap: 10 mTorr, 30 sccm, or 10 min argon plasma

fresh/crystallization/B1.q: What bond dissociation energy does the Sn-incorporated GST terahertz study give for the Sn–Te bond?

fresh/crystallization/T1.q: At 1 THz, what refractive index and real permittivity did the Sn24W-GST film annealed at 250 °C have?

fresh/crystallization/C2.q: At what temperatures and for how long were the GST and Sn-incorporated GST thin films annealed in the terahertz metasurface study?
fresh/crystallization/C2.expect: 150 and 250 °C for 15 min on a hot plate (sec. 2)

fresh/crystallization/X1.q: In the Sn-incorporated GST terahertz study, by what factor did the 1 THz conductivity of undoped GST rise from annealing at 150 °C to annealing at 250 °C?

fresh/crystallization/H1.q: Which GST thin film in the Sn-incorporated GST terahertz study had the highest conductivity at 1 THz, and what power was its Sn target sputtered at?
fresh/crystallization/H1.expect: Sn24W-GST-250 (σ 17928.63); Sn target at 24 W (Table 1, sec. 2)

fresh/crystallization/F1.q: Why does Sn incorporation raise the crystallization temperature of Ge2Sb2Te5 thin films in the terahertz sensing study?
fresh/crystallization/F1.expect: It does not: Sn lowers the effective crystallization temperature, forming SnTe and SnSb phases with weaker bonds (abstract, sec. 3.1)

fresh/crystallization/A1.q: What switching time does the Sn-incorporated GST terahertz metasurface achieve between its amorphous and crystalline states?
fresh/crystallization/A1.expect: Not given: the films were switched by 15 min hot-plate annealing and the metasurface was simulated; no switching time is reported
fresh/crystallization/A1.trap: the 15 min anneal or the 0.16 THz shift given as a switching time

fresh/reactor/C1.q: In the review of lithium-mediated ammonia electrosynthesis, what shares of global energy consumption and of global CO2 emissions are attributed to the Haber–Bosch process?
fresh/reactor/C1.expect: about 2% of global energy consumption and 1.8% of global CO2 emissions (sec. 1)

fresh/reactor/B1.q: In the review of lithium-mediated ammonia electrosynthesis, what ammonia faradaic efficiency did LiTFSI give in the gas diffusion electrode flow electrolyser with a PtAu anode?
fresh/reactor/B1.expect: 18%, because sulfur-based decomposition products poisoned the PtAu HOR catalyst (sec. on reactor design)

fresh/reactor/T1.q: In the lithium-mediated ammonia review's comparison of electrolysers, what faradaic efficiency, yield rate and stability does the two-compartment batch cell with LiNTf2/NH3/THF reach?
fresh/reactor/T1.trap: the single-compartment LiNTf2 C2H5OH/THF cell's 100%, 150, 96 h

fresh/reactor/T2.q: In the lithium-mediated ammonia review's comparison of electrolysers, which electrolyte does the gas diffusion electrode flow cell with 300 h stability use, and what faradaic and energy efficiencies does it reach?
fresh/reactor/T2.expect: LiBF4 in C2H5OH/DG (diglyme); FE 64%, EE 17% (at −6 mA cm−2) (Table 1)

fresh/reactor/X1.q: In the lithium-mediated ammonia review's comparison of electrolysers, what is the mean faradaic efficiency of the gas diffusion electrode flow cells?
fresh/reactor/X1.trap: including the MEA reactor (9%) or the Pd membrane (36%)

fresh/reactor/H1.q: Which configuration in the lithium-mediated ammonia review's comparison of electrolysers has the lowest faradaic efficiency, and what electrolyte does it use?
fresh/reactor/H1.expect: the MEA reactor, 9%; a PEO polymer electrolyte (lithium-doped) (Table 1)
fresh/reactor/H1.trap: the single-compartment cell's 33% or the GDE cell's 35%

fresh/reactor/F1.q: Why does the Haber–Bosch process, as described in the lithium-mediated ammonia review, run at pressures of only 1-5 atm?
fresh/reactor/F1.expect: It does not: it runs at 200-400 atm and 400-650 °C (sec. 1)

fresh/reactor/A1.q: What production cost per tonne of ammonia does the review of lithium-mediated ammonia electrosynthesis give for Li-NRR?
fresh/reactor/A1.expect: Not given: the review states no ammonia cost
fresh/reactor/A1.trap: an efficiency or yield rate given as a cost

fresh/mass-transfer/C1.q: In the photocatalytic ozonation of antibiotics with bimetallic Pd/Cu on rutile TiO2 and g-C3N4, what gas flow rate, inlet ozone concentration and catalyst loading were used?

fresh/mass-transfer/B1.q: In the photocatalytic ozonation study of Pd/Cu-modified rutile TiO2 and g-C3N4, how many times higher than ozonation alone was the sulfamethoxazole pseudo-first-order rate constant of (Pd/Cu)TiO2 at 1% loading?

fresh/mass-transfer/T1.q: What Pd and Cu contents did XPS give for the (Pd/Cu)1%TiO2 photocatalyst in the photocatalytic ozonation study?

fresh/mass-transfer/T2.q: What carbon and nitrogen contents did XPS give for the (Pd/Cu)0.5%C3N4 photocatalyst used for photocatalytic ozonation?

fresh/mass-transfer/X1.q: In the photocatalytic ozonation study with Pd/Cu-modified TiO2 and g-C3N4, how much ozone was fed to the reactor per minute?

fresh/mass-transfer/H1.q: Which bimetallic loading does the Pd/Cu photocatalytic ozonation study find indispensable for suppressing bacterial regrowth after treatment, and what average particle diameter did the TiO2 catalyst at that loading have?

fresh/mass-transfer/F1.q: Why did ozonation alone fully degrade sulfamethoxazole within 5 min in the photocatalytic ozonation study of Pd/Cu-modified TiO2 and g-C3N4?
fresh/mass-transfer/F1.expect: It did not: ozonation alone gave 50% degradation in 30 min; photocatalytic ozonation gave full degradation after 5 min (sec. 3.2)

fresh/mass-transfer/A1.q: What TOC removal did the photocatalytic ozonation of sulfamethoxazole with Pd/Cu-modified TiO2 and g-C3N4 reach?
fresh/mass-transfer/A1.expect: Not given: no TOC, DOC or COD removal is reported
fresh/mass-transfer/A1.trap: the 50% SMX degradation or full degradation in 5 min given as TOC removal
